position blocks that are not in train

in the code. It is ‘supported’ if the seed-mean Δ ≥ 0.02, the seeds with Δ > 0 are ≥ 4/5, and, when an interval can be computed (every seed has ≥ 8 test clusters), the lower bound of the 95% interval is > 0. Otherwise it is ‘not supported’. The interval is a group bootstrap over position blocks, it is conditional, and it cannot reflect the overlap between seeds.
The settings fixed for demonstration are block 10, Ridge and the last layer. Sensitivity looks at block sizes {3, 5, 10} and is for reporting.

Accountability: since this is protein stability prediction, the dual-use risk is judged to be low †. Checking institutional policy is assumed to be not applicable. The license of the DMS data must be checked before release.

: the interpretation that the high score in the random split is explained by the position effect (100% of test positions are in train) is consistent with the leakage table above, but no experiment to separate the factors was done. Limitations and what was not done

children.label: Limitations and what was not done

children.value: Only one assay and 8M were covered, and only Ridge and the last layer were used. There are 5 seeds, and because the split repeats have overlapping test sets, they are not independent repeats.
Because there are only 2–6 test clusters, no interval was computed.

There are 5 random-init controls and one pretrained model. The number of training variants differs by split (random ≈ 806, position-block ≈ 700). The license of the DMS data is unverified. The dual-use review is at the descriptive level. No independent review was received.
